problem: Embodied navigation research is fragmented: separate specialized architectures for Point-Goal, Object-Goal, instruction-following, POI-Goal and person-following, which blocks cross-task generalization and sharing of a unified physical prior from heterogeneous data.
motivation: Real-world missions mix approaching, reaching and interaction phases, so a single generalist navigator is needed. Large-scale unified data (indoor and outdoor, sim, video and real robot) plus reasoning supervision could yield a foundation model that generalizes and deploys on real robots.
key_idea: A single Brain-Action VLA (Qwen3-4B LLM with a flow-matching action expert) trained on 16.9M unified trajectories plus 5M reasoning samples covers five navigation tasks, and is wrapped in an agentic planner with topological memory for real deployment.
insight: The paper has no ablations, so the causes are asserted rather than demonstrated. The authors attribute the gains to the reasoning-plus-action split and to joint multi-task, indoor-outdoor training. The clearest evidence is the small gap on OVON, where SR drops only 1.3 from Val-Seen to Val-Unseen, versus 14.2 for MTU3D. The system design also rests on the observation that Reaching tasks degrade over long horizons while Point-Goal stays robust, hence the coarse-to-fine planner.
method: Universal Multi-Modal Encoder: ViT encodes RGB in panoramic mode (left/front/right views fed separately with view tokens) or front-only mode, plus a visual history buffer. Text goals go through the LLM tokenizer; point goals (x,y) go through an MLP into pseudo-tokens.

Cognitive Brain: Qwen3-4B with task-conditional Reasoning Head or Action Head (If-Else on the task token, not serial CoT). Auxiliary reasoning tasks (traversable-area polygons, social CoT, milestone CoT, POI grounding, VQA) shape the latent context.
Action Expert: Flow Matching head conditioned on the Brain, predicting 5 waypoints (x,y,yaw) in the local BEV frame, chosen to model multi-modal expert behaviours.

Data Engine: 7,802 scenes (6.25 km2 indoor, 4.42 km2 outdoor, 3DGS scans, HM3D, InteriorGS, SocCity). 16.9M trajectories: 4.0M point-goal (2.0M internet-video pseudo-trajectories, 1.7M sim, 340K real robot), instruction following (R2R/RxR 1.5M, door traversal 0.3M, person search 0.2M, short-horizon 0.8M), object-goal (HM3D/OVON 1.8M, OVON-sub 0.2M, InteriorGS 1.6M), POI 2.5M (Wan2.1-generated videos), person-following 4.0M. Plus 5.0M reasoning samples.

Three-stage training: (1) Cognitive warm-up: NTP on reasoning data, with vision encoder and action expert frozen. (2) Unified SFT: joint NTP + conditional flow matching loss, with a ~20% reasoning replay buffer. (3) SAFE-GRPO: flow-based RL that updates only the Action Expert on SocCity, with social-compliance, expert-similarity, smoothness and efficiency rewards.

Agentic Navigation System: a cloud VLM Planner decomposes intents into Point/Object/POI/Instruction/Person sub-tasks (coarse-to-fine). A hierarchical Topo-Memory (block, road, function, object/POI layers, AMAP routing) supports planning. A Self-Reflector triggers re-planning on failure.

Edge deployment: SigLIP-B/16 (93M) with token merging (merge size 4) runs at 2Hz on a Jetson Orin NX, with about a 3% performance drop. A CE-Nav-based Neural Controller runs at over 10Hz, converting waypoints to velocities on a Unitree Go2.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-4B LLM + ViT encoder + flow-matching action expert (fine-tuned); planner is a separate cloud VLM
setting.training_data: 16.9M expert trajectories (sim scenes, internet-video pseudo-trajectories, real robot logs, Wan2.1-generated videos) + 5.0M reasoning/VQA samples; SAFE-GRPO RL in SocCity
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (left/front/right) or front RGB plus visual history; no depth or odometry in benchmarks
setting.action_space: predicted waypoints (5 x (x,y,yaw)) in the local BEV frame, tracked by a velocity controller on the real robot
setting.simulator: Habitat (VLN-CE, OVON), SocCity, EVT-Bench, CityWalker open-loop, BridgeNav, Isaac Sim (controller RL)

numbers_note: No ablations reported. Split names for non-canonical benchmarks (CityWalker, SocNav, BridgeNav, EVT-Bench) are assumed as 'test'. The paper does not state the split explicitly.
results: A single model sets SOTA on 7 benchmarks: R2R-CE SR 66.4 / SPL 63.9 (vs NavFoM 61.7 / 55.3), RxR-CE SR 69.3 (vs 64.4), and OVON Val-Unseen SR 54.0 (vs NavFoM 45.2, MTU3D 40.8). It also reaches SocNav SR 88.3 vs CityWalker 47.8, and the best EVT-Bench SR/TR (AT SR 67.3 vs TrackVLA++ 51.2). Losses: OVON Val-Unseen SPL (30.5 vs NavFoM 31.9) and EVT-Bench collision rate.
limitations: No ablations of the data, reasoning, training stages or SAFE-GRPO, so the causes of the gains are not isolated; the trained models and the proprietary data are not clearly released.
Collision rate on EVT-Bench is much worse than TrackVLA/TrackVLA++, and OVON Val-Unseen SPL is slightly below NavFoM.
Real-world results are qualitative only, with no quantitative real-robot metrics; the edge model loses about 3% performance.
